title: Embedding a Silent Machine with Return State
statement: Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $\iota$ inject the $m$ work-tape indices into the $k$ work-tape indices, and choose one of the $k$ indices as a distinguished tape. From an $m$-tape Turing machine with state set $S$, form a $k$-tape machine with states $S\sqcup\{\ast\}$, where $\ast$ is a new state. Its initial state is the original initial state. In an original state, it reads the symbols on tapes selected by $\iota$, applies the original transition, embeds that action using the distinguished tape, and sends a halting transition to $\ast$ instead of halting. In state $\ast$, it stays on the input, makes no work-tape writes or head movements, emits no symbol, and transitions to $\ast$.
hypotheses_covered: An injection from the $m$ tape indices into the $k$ tape indices
A distinguished index among the $k$ tapes
An $m$-tape Turing machine with state set $S`
caveat: The definition of the action-embedding operation is not included, so the distinguished-tape convention cannot be fully specified.
